title: 5 Fantastic Dividend Stocks You May Be Overlooking
author: Keith Speights
description: The article highlights five underrated dividend stocks offering attractive yields: Ares Capital (9.9% yield, 69 consecutive quarters of maintained/grown dividends), Bristol Myers Squibb (4% yield, 17 consecutive years of increases despite patent cliff concerns), Edison International (5.9% yield, 22 consecutive years of increases but facing wildfire litigation), MPLX LP (8.5% yield with 12.5% annual distribution growth), and NNN REIT (6% yield with 37 consecutive years of dividend increases, outperforming Realty Income).

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Maintains strong 9.9% dividend yield with 69 consecutive quarters of maintained or grown dividends. Largest publicly traded BDC with highly diversified portfolio of 636 businesses, reducing concentration risk.

Offers attractive 4% yield with 94 consecutive years of dividend payments and 17 consecutive years of increases. Growth portfolio now represents 59% of revenue with strong pipeline of 30+ late-stage programs offsetting patent cliff concerns.

Offers attractive 4% yield with 94 consecutive years of dividend payments and 17 consecutive years of increases. Growth portfolio now represents 59% of revenue with strong pipeline of 30+ late-stage programs offsetting patent cliff concerns.

Provides 5.9% yield with 22 consecutive years of dividend increases and low 37% payout ratio. However, stock is down 20% from peak due to wildfire litigation risks, though potential California liability reform could provide relief.

Offers one of the highest midstream yields at 8.5% with 12.5% annual distribution growth over three years. Benefits from strong tailwind in data center demand for natural gas and is investing in pipeline expansion.

Provides 6% yield with 37 consecutive years of dividend increases (longer than Realty Income). Safe dividend with 68% AFFO payout ratio, well-diversified portfolio with no tenant exceeding 5% of rent, and 88.7% of revenue from defensive retail sectors.
Mentioned as popular REIT but article positions NNN REIT as superior alternative with higher yield (6% vs 5.5%) and longer dividend increase streak (37 vs unspecified years).

title: Entergy Q3 Earnings Top Estimates, Revenues Increase Year Over Year
author: Na
description: Entergy Corporation reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.98 per share, beating estimates by 15.8% with a 29.4% year-over-year increase. Revenues rose 14.5% to $4.37 billion, driven by higher electricity demand and 7.4% retail sales growth. The company narrowed its 2026 guidance to $4.35-$4.45 per share and maintained its target of over 8% annual earnings growth through 2030, supported by a $55 billion capital investment plan for 2027-2030.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q3 earnings beat (15.8% above consensus), significant year-over-year EPS growth (29.4%), revenue outperformance (5.1% above estimate), and narrowed guidance with improved lower bound. Utility segment showed robust performance with higher electricity sales and regulatory recoveries. Long-term growth outlook remains solid with 8%+ annual earnings growth target through 2030.

Despite beating EPS estimates by 4.9%, the company experienced significant year-over-year earnings decline (17.9%) and revenue miss (11.7% below consensus). Operating revenues also declined 15% year-over-year, indicating weakening operational performance.

title: Edison International: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
author: The Motley Fool Team
description: Edison International reaffirmed its 2026 core EPS guidance of $5.90-$6.20 on its Q3 earnings call. The company faces challenges from delayed California wildfire liability reform, which threatens to increase financing costs and force SCE to curb clean energy investments during its 2029 rate case. However, SCE has hardened 90% of its distribution network in high fire areas and plans $38-41 billion in capital spending through 2030 without issuing common stock, targeting 5-7% annual earnings growth.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company reaffirmed guidance and demonstrated operational progress with grid hardening achievements and a solid capital plan. However, delayed wildfire liability reform creates significant headwinds that could force reductions in clean energy investments and increase borrowing costs, creating uncertainty for long-term growth despite management's confidence in execution.

title: Edison International Q3 Earnings Outpace Estimates, Revenues Miss
author: Na
description: Edison International (EIX) reported Q3 2026 core EPS of $1.92, beating estimates by 4.9%, but revenues of $4.89 billion missed by 11.7%. Southern California Edison's earnings declined 17.9% year-over-year due to absence of prior-year GRC benefits. EIX reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $5.90-$6.20 EPS and maintained 5-7% annual earnings growth target through 2030.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed results with EPS beat offset by significant revenue miss and 17.9% year-over-year earnings decline. However, reaffirmed guidance and maintained growth targets provide some confidence, resulting in a neutral outlook.

title: EIX Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Urgency of Wildfire Reform
author: Na
description: Edison International (EIX) reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance of $5.90-$6.20 and 5%-7% annual core earnings growth through 2030, while emphasizing the urgent need for California wildfire liability reform. The company faces rising infrastructure financing costs potentially reaching $300 million due to elevated credit spreads, and is managing Eaton Fire liabilities with over $1.1 billion in settlement offers extended. EIX plans $38B-$41B in capital spending through 2030 while advancing grid hardening efforts.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: EIX reaffirmed positive earnings guidance and demonstrated operational stability with Q3 core earnings beating estimates. However, this is offset by significant headwinds including Eaton Fire liabilities, rising financing costs ($300M impact), potential capital spending constraints, and regulatory uncertainty around wildfire reform. The company's Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with weak momentum (Score F) reflects this mixed outlook.
